rule: A ✓ means a published, machine-checked proof shows that all the code computing the operation, as that library runs it on that host, gives the specified result for every input: the cipher and its mode, the hash over every block with its padding, the whole scalar multiplication or exponentiation, and the glue around them, such as clamping, byte conversion, and point encoding. Parsing DER key and signature containers, randomness, and the message hash a signature takes are left out. Proofs of memory safety alone, or of only some of the code, earn no ✓.

hosts.name: kixtop
hosts.note: The maintainer's MacBook, in daily use. Its cores have DIT, and this run timed rind two ways. The AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, header protection, SHA-2, HMAC, and HKDF rows hold `rind::cpu::Dit::hold()` across calls, as MoQ does and as the report's rind column assumes. rind's other rows set DIT around each call. In the other primitive rows that toggle cost 20 to 120 ns a call in the run before, so their times overstate rind's. In the rustls rows, holding DIT would also run rustls' own code with it on, a cost not yet measured, so which way they would move is open.

groups.name: Not ranked: RSA key generation: its time varies too much from run to run to rank
Not ranked: a JWT's `load` rows: aws-lc-rs's provider parses the key only when it signs or verifies, so only `token`, which includes loading, compares
Not ranked: blind RSA, OPRF, VRF, SPAKE2+, and Argon2id: neither aws-lc-rs nor ring offers the protocol, so there is no baseline, and the report's hosts compare it

gaps.reason: Without SSE4.1 rind runs Graviola's scalar Poly1305 rather than port BoringSSL's SSE2 `poly1305_vec.c` for CPUs older than Westmere, as ALGORITHMS.md records.
AES header protection on aarch64 reaches the key's cipher through an indirect call, as ALGORITHMS.md notes, which costs 3.5 ns against aws-lc-rs's 2.8 ns for one block.

Not rind's hashing: `kixtop`'s data is its run on [`0d2e74b4`](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/commit/0d2e74b489c1067beeab373f9de75d24574b4bc5), from before rind's rows held DIT, and these rows had no DIT-held time, so they include rind's per-call DIT toggle (about 35 ns of 166 and 170 ns) that the other libraries never pay. `kixtop` was offline for this refresh; its next run times rind holding DIT and rechecks them.

P-521 ECDH with a stored key on the portable backend, fiat-crypto's arithmetic on 64-bit limbs, measured 1.12× aws-lc's C without assembly in [run 43646114817](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/actions/runs/43646114817), where [#614](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/614)'s measurement on a shared x86_64 host had P-521 ECDH at 0.91 to 1.03×, and the ephemeral-key row is within 10% in the same run. Rare on targets without assembly; the next refresh rechecks it.

The portable backend runs aws-lc's `aes_nohw.c` in its 64-bit configuration, four blocks a pass ([#621](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/621)), while this row builds aws-lc's C for x86_64, where it bitslices eight blocks into SSE2 registers: the configuration aws-lc itself runs on the other 64-bit targets the backend is for is rind's. In [run 43646114817](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/actions/runs/43646114817) AES-GCM measured 1.10 to 1.21× from 1200 B, AES-CTR 1.26 to 1.45×, and CBC decryption 1.14 to 1.24×; shorter messages are within 10%.

rind's portable SHA-1 trails aws-lc's C by 1.1 to 1.25× from 1200 B up, as it still did in [run 43282064559](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/actions/runs/43282064559) on a later main. SHA-1 survives only for legacy signatures and HMAC-SHA-1, which are rare on targets without assembly, so it stays rather than take aws-lc's integer `sha1_block_data_order_nohw`, which armv7 without NEON already runs, as a speed quest.

quest.title: The portable backend's SHA-256 and SHA-512 run the fastest permissive source
armv7 without the crypto extension runs aws-lc's NEON AES and GHASH

gaps.reason: Unwrapping a 16-byte key takes 35 to 55 ns more than aws-lc-rs's 280 to 400 ns on the EPYC runners of [run 43646114817](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/actions/runs/43646114817), 1.11 to 1.20× its time; wrapping, every longer key, and the other x86_64 tiers are within 10%, armv7 NEON unwraps it in about 2.02× and has its own decision above, and aarch64 unwraps in 0.68× aws-lc-rs's time. Key wrap is rare and runs once per stored key, so the fixed cost stays without a quest; the next refresh rechecks it.

Decided in [kixel-ai/rind#812](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/812): on x86_64 without AVX-512, ML-KEM-768 key generation stays on rind's arithmetic though pyca/verified-garbage's is faster, since a key pair decapsulates on the arithmetic that generated it and VG's decapsulation was 1.17 to 1.25× slower there when it decided (1.09 to 1.22× in these runs), and decapsulation is the hot path.

quest.title: ristretto255's variable-base multiplication runs curve25519-dalek's AVX2 formulas

gaps.reason: Closed after this run: [kixel-ai/rind#847](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/847), which landed after the run's commit, takes pyca/verified-garbage's `d·G` for each signature's `k·G` on x86_64 and aarch64, which measured faster than rind's comb. The next refresh measures it.

SHA3-512 at 16 KB measured 1.16× pyca/verified-garbage's time (110.7 against 95.7 µs; aws-lc-rs 103.3), while SHA3-256 at 16 KB is level (53.7 µs both). x86_64 runs one Keccak-f on every CPU, and [kixel-ai/rind#851](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/851) kept rind's proven one, since VG measured 1.01 to 1.05× rind's time from 1200 B on Zen 3 and Zen 4. The next refresh rechecks it.

Closed after this run: pyca/verified-garbage measured 30.6 µs against rind's 38.2 µs (aws-lc-rs 38.0) on `nixos`'s Zen 3, and [kixel-ai/rind#846](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/846), which landed after the run's commit, verifies with VG's routine on x86_64 with BMI2 and ADX. The next refresh measures it.

Noise: CI jobs on `nixos` kept about 4 CPUs busy through this run, and a second run of the same commit right after it, under more load elsewhere, measured each of these within 10% of the fastest: PKCS#1 signing 0.97× graviola's time (PSS signing 0.94× in this run), ChaCha20-Poly1305 bulk 1.03× ring's, the resumed handshake 1.00× graviola's, and SHA3-256 and SHA3-512 at 16 KB 0.96 and 1.04× aws-lc-rs's. The next refresh rechecks them.
